My mother, Audrey Marie Murray, was in the Empire State Building when the plane hit.
She told me the story over a hundred times.
She was just 19 years old and it was her first real job as a secretary.
She was working for the Office of War Information (OWI).
She had come in on Saturday to catch up on work, and there were a few people with her in the office.
She told me that she saw the plane flying straight towards her floor, and at the last second, the plane swerved up and hit the "Catholic Charity's" floor... just one floor above.
Every one in the Office of War Information survived.

In 1945, my mother was 11 years old.
One of her uncles died in Germany during the war.
She remembered saving rubber and scraps of metal, like aluminum for the government to use to manufacture things that were in short supply during the war.
She said that women couldn't get nylons, because the government needed all of the nylon that was available to make parachutes for the military.
She said that some food products were scarce.
American companies like Nabisco and Hershey's got millions of dollars for their products from the government to supply the American servicemen with crackers, cookies and candy during the war.
